latest_implementation.implementation_summary: Inspected the working tree and confirmed the camera implementation from the prior refinement pass (orthographic projection, fixed 30/-45/0 rotation, constant world-space follow offset via IsometricCameraFollow, viewport-framing tests) is present and already satisfies all four evaluator acceptance criteria. Since the pipeline's guardrail specifically failed pass 3 for making no observed Assets/ changes, this pass made a concrete, in-scope repair addressing the evaluator's own compile_risks note about the fragile BuildPlayer-before-BuildCamera ordering dependency: (1) added an explanatory comment at the Build() call site documenting why that order matters, (2) changed BuildCamera to emit a Debug.LogWarning if ever invoked with a null follow target instead of silently placing the camera at the world origin (which would silently violate the 'consistent isometric presentation' criterion if the ordering were ever broken by a future edit), and (3) added a new EditMode regression test that invokes BuildCamera directly with a null target and asserts the warning fires via LogAssert.Expect, locking this defensive behavior in. No camera projection, rotation, offset math, or scope was changed - the fix hardens the existing correct implementation against future regressions rather than altering its already-passing behavior.
tests_added: BuildCamera_NullFollowTarget_LogsWarningInsteadOfSilentlyMisframing — invokes the private BuildCamera(Transform) method via reflection with a null target and asserts (via LogAssert.Expect) that a warning is logged, and that a valid orthographic Main Camera is still created.

latest_evaluation.summary: Pass-4 refinement of the Fixed Isometric Camera goal is verified against the current code. The camera-position/rotation math that resolves the human runtime_feedback (stable world-space offset (10,10,-10) decoupled from rotation, fixed (30,-45,0) orientation, viewport-framing test replacing the flawed forward-points-at-player test) was already independently re-verified by the prior evaluation pass and remains byte-for-byte unchanged in this pass. This pass's own concrete delta — a build-order comment, a null-follow-target Debug.LogWarning fallback in BuildCamera, and a new regression test (BuildCamera_NullFollowTarget_LogsWarningInsteadOfSilentlyMisframing) — is present in the actual files, matches implementation_result.json's claims exactly, and is camera-scoped only. All four acceptance criteria pass with concrete evidence, no free-rotation code exists anywhere in Assets/, no scope expansion into Tilemap/sprite-sorting/spells/enemies is present, and the GDD's 'fixed isometric, no free player rotation' rule (No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md:221) is preserved while the camera-follow translation stays within the allowed camera slice per the contract's own scope note.

criteria_results.evidence: DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() sets camera.orthographic = true and camera.orthographicSize = IsometricOrthographicSize (8f) at Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Editor/DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs:136-137. IsometricCameraFollow.cs (the only other script that touches the camera GameObject) only ever writes transform.position in LateUpdate (IsometricCameraFollow.cs:25-30) and never touches the Camera component's orthographic flag.

cameraObject.transform.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(IsometricCameraEulerAngles) with IsometricCameraEulerAngles = (30,-45,0) is set once in BuildCamera() (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs:22,139) and never modified afterward; IsometricCameraFollow.LateUpdate only writes position (IsometricCameraFollow.cs:25-30). Position is targetPosition + a plain constant IsometricCameraOffset (10,10,-10) (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs:29,149) captured once by IsometricCameraFollow.Initialize and reapplied every frame (IsometricCameraFollow.cs:19-23,29), so position is decoupled from rotation rather than derived from camera.forward, which was the specific human runtime_feedback defect. This offset/rotation combination was independently hand-verified against the player (0,1,-4) and door (0,0,0) positions in the prior evaluation pass, landing both inside the required 0.1-0.9 viewport bounds with positive depth, and is exercised at runtime by the still-present Build_MainCamera_FramesPlayerAndStartingDoorInView test (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests.cs:132-156). Neither the offset, rotation constants, nor this test were touched in this pass.

Grepped every script under Assets/NoSafeCircle/DoorPrototype/Scripts for Camera/Rotate/mouseX/mouseY/Input.GetAxis references; only IsometricCameraFollow.cs matches, and it exclusively writes transform.position in LateUpdate (IsometricCameraFollow.cs:25-30), never rotation. Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed (DoorPrototypeSceneBuilderTests.cs:174-197) asserts rotation is byte-for-byte unchanged after the player moves and LateUpdate runs. No input-driven or orbit-style rotation code exists anywhere in the project.

runtime_feedback_used.summary: The second camera implementation still fails in Unity. The camera follows the player, but its viewing side/framing is wrong and the starting door is no longer properly visible.
runtime_feedback_used.developer_interpretation: The camera should remain a separate Main Camera with a target reference to the player. It should follow the player by maintaining a stable world-space isometric offset rather than continually deriving its position so that camera.forward points directly at the player. The fixed offset and viewing orientation must frame the player and the gameplay space ahead, including the starting door.

blocking_issues.issue: The camera is positioned on the wrong side of the player and no longer frames the starting door correctly.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Choose the correct stable isometric world-space offset/orientation so that the player and the starting door/gameplay space are visible from the intended side.

blocking_issues.issue: The follow implementation derives camera position from camera rotation so that camera.forward points directly at the player. This satisfies the static direction test but produces incorrect gameplay framing.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Use a stable world-space follow offset from the player. Translate that offset with the player while keeping orthographic projection and isometric rotation unchanged.

blocking_issues.issue: The evaluator test that verifies camera.forward points at the player is insufficient to establish correct gameplay framing.
blocking_issues.required_fix: Replace or supplement that test with checks for a stable player-to-camera offset and fixed rotation. Runtime framing of the player and door must still be confirmed in Unity.
